summary: ```markdown # Quick Start Tutorial on Physical Properties and Importing Settings into Unreal ## Overview Welcome to the quick start tutorial on physical properties and importing settings into Unreal. This guide covers the essential aspects of using fabric parameters set in Marvelous Designer when working with Unreal Engine. ## USD Export and Fabric Parameters During USD export, if "Include garment simulation data" is selected, Unreal Engine's Chaos Cloth will be able to reuse the fabric parameters set in Marvelous Designer. ## Physical Property Menu By selecting the fabric, you can scroll down to see the physical property menu. The key properties include: ### Stretch - **Definition**: Stretch refers to how the fabric will stretch. - **Values**: Lower values provide more elasticity, while higher values result in a stiffer fabric. ### Density - **Adjustment**: By adjusting the density, I can make the fabric heavier to better demonstrate its properties. ### Bending - **Definition**: The bending of a fabric is its stiffness. - **Values**: Higher values result in a narrower fabric that is stiff and will not bend as easily compared to fabrics with lower values. ### Buckling Ratio - **Definition**: The buckling ratio reflects the fabric's tendency to preserve its shape when force is applied. - **Demonstration**: This property is best demonstrated by selecting different fabric presets. ### Buckling Stiffness - **Usage**: Buckling stiffness is used alongside bending weft and warp. The higher the buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the ends of the fabric. ## Fabric Comparison Here I will compare silk and leather. By selecting the pattern piece, you can adjust the simulation properties. ### Additional Thickness - **Adjustment**: Adjusting the additional thickness will result in the fabric resting further or closer to the avatar. ### Layers - **Definition**: Layers are used to indicate where a pattern sits in relation to others. - **Hierarchy**: Zero is the base, and any pattern with a higher number will sit atop a lower numbered pattern. ## Weft and Warp - **Weft**: Affects the horizontal size of the fabric. - **Warp**: Affects the vertical size of the fabric. - **Shrinkage**: Weft and warp settings can shrink or enlarge the pattern. ### Pressure Setting - **Function**: The pressure setting will make a pattern blow up or suck in, depending on the size of the pattern. ### Overhead and Weft Variations - **Overhead**: Used to create a wafer pattern on overhanging fabric. - **Weft Variations**: Allows us to create patterns exposed to soil or with specific shapes. ## Simulation Properties To store the pattern, weft will show how the pattern is performed. If you want to add a pattern, weft can be set at the center of the weft with the right-hand overhanging fabric. These patterns are found in the bottom weft and are also available in the top weft. ### Stitching and Vertical Patterns Wefts are used for stitching. The vertical pattern can be set higher than the horizontal pattern. ## Exporting to Unreal Engine Remember, when exporting, to check the "Include garment simulation data" box to retain these settings for use in Unreal Engine. ### Simulation Effects During simulation, gravity will affect how a garment falls, with the default value of -9.800 being closest to real life. ### Air Damping - **Effect**: Air damping will make moving garments slow down as if underwater when set to values higher than 1. ### Timestep - **Adjustments**: The timestep will affect the time used to calculate the simulation. ## Limitations and Future Updates Not all simulation data exported from Marvelous Designer can be used in Unreal Engine yet. However, more simulation data will be available for export in the future as this feature is upgraded. ## Conclusion Thanks for watching! ```
